name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 15 points and Erin Houchin is the incumbent
Houchin holds an overwhelming money edge: $1.86M raised and $1.18M on hand versus about $105K for Brad Meyer
Prediction markets price Houchin's win chance near 96 percent
No public polling and no expert ratings; the challenger lacks resources to change the race
model.rationale: The 9th District's strong Republican lean, Houchin's incumbency, and her roughly eighteen-to-one fundraising advantage over Brad Meyer leave little room for an upset, and prediction markets agree at about 96 percent Republican. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which all point the same direction.
model.watch: A sharp national Democratic wave or a sudden influx of outside spending against Houchin could narrow the margin, though flipping the outcome would require an extraordinary shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin enters the general election as a heavy favorite in southern Indiana's 9th District, a seat that leans Republican by fifteen points. She won renomination and has built a dominant financial position, raising about 1.86 million dollars with 1.18 million still on hand. Democratic nominee Brad Meyer has raised roughly 105 thousand dollars and had about 18 thousand on hand in the latest filings, leaving little capacity to introduce himself to voters. A Libertarian candidate has minimal funds and is unlikely to affect the result.

No public polls of the race are available and no expert raters have ranked it, but prediction markets put Houchin's chances near 96 percent. District lean, incumbency, and money all point the same direction, making the real question the size of the Republican margin rather than the winner.
